title: My AI Adoption Journey
author: Mitchell Hashimoto
claims: Hashimoto reports that he adds repository instruction entries for recurring command or API mistakes and adds executable checks for mistakes that a tool can detect.
limits: Self-report. No controlled benchmark or requirement to use several simultaneous agents. The trace rollup contract and gate are proposed adaptations.
evidence: Step 5: Engineer the Harness, the two items under This comes in two forms. Step 2, the numbered list after his repeated-commit exercise. Step 6, the paragraph about preferring one agent.

title: Ghostty inspector repository instructions
author: Ghostty contributors
claims: The inspector instructions identify a generated C header, an upstream widget demonstration, a macOS build flag, and the lack of package unit tests.
limits: One subsystem at one revision. The trace rollup package uses a different language, entry point, and tests.
evidence: src/inspector/AGENTS.md, all four bullets below Inspector Subsystem.

title: Red/green TDD
author: Simon Willison
claims: Willison advises a test-first cycle. Observe the test fail before a code change so that green can demonstrate a behavior change.
limits: The chapter describes a method. It supplies no effect size for this workshop. Trace fixture choices and the expected output here are original.
evidence: Red/green TDD, the paragraph that begins with the most disciplined form of TDD and the paragraph on what can happen if the red phase is skipped.

title: Pi: The Minimal Agent Within OpenClaw
author: Armin Ronacher
claims: Ronacher describes a fresh review context inside Pi's session tree and carries review results back to the main session.
limits: A session branch and a Git worktree solve different problems. The workshop's separate test branch and local merge gate are proposed adaptations. The Pi command was not run here.
evidence: The /review subsection, the paragraph on a fresh context and the paragraph that lists review targets.

title: Pi code review extension
author: Armin Ronacher and contributors
version: main, unpinned snapshot inspected for this edition
claims: The TypeScript extension builds different review prompts by Git target. A branch prompt uses a resolved merge base when one is available. A separate explicit option controls inclusion of local changes.
limits: The source can change on main. Review heuristics in the extension do not demonstrate correctness on a given patch. The workshop uses a local pinned diff and executable cases without this extension.
evidence: extensions/review.ts, ReviewTarget, getMergeBase, and buildReviewPrompt. Inspect the baseBranch switch arm and includeLocalChanges.

title: git-worktree
author: Git contributors
claims: Git can attach multiple working trees to one repository. Linked trees have independent working files, indexes and HEADs. Most refs are shared.
limits: A worktree grants no process isolation. The workshop uses separate temporary paths and no shared output resource.
evidence: DESCRIPTION, COMMANDS add, and DETAILS. In DETAILS inspect the GIT_DIR and GIT_COMMON_DIR examples.
